cards.text: Jesus is gaining and baptizing more disciples than John the Baptist, and the Pharisees, a group of strict religious leaders, are aware of it. Jesus realizes they know. Word travels fast, friend, even without a group chat.

cards.question: Jesus Himself is the one doing all the baptizing.

cards.text: So Jesus leaves Judea and returns to Galilee. No car, no GPS, no lady in the dashboard sighing 'recalculating' every five minutes.

cards.question: To get from Judea back to Galilee, Jesus has to pass through ___.

cards.text: He comes to a town of Samaria called Sychar. It's near the plot of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.

cards.question: Jacob's well is in Sychar, and Jesus is ___ from His journey, so He sits down by the well.

cards.text: It's about the sixth hour when a Samaritan woman comes to draw water. And Jesus is the one who speaks first.

cards.question: What does Jesus, sitting tired by the well, say to the Samaritan woman?
Jesus's disciples are right there beside Him at the well when He talks to the woman.

cards.text: "You are a Jew," said the woman. You know the face you make when someone who has NEVER said a word to you suddenly asks you for a favor? I bet she's making THAT face.

cards.question: Why is the Samaritan woman so surprised that this Jewish man asks her for a drink?

answers.text: Jews do not associate with Samaritans
Men never come to draw at this well
She has no jar to draw water with

cards.text: Jesus answered, "If you knew the gift of God and who is asking you for a drink, you would have asked Him, and He would have given you living water." Hold on. The thirsty guy is now the one talking about GIVING water.

cards.question: The woman points out a problem with Jesus getting this living water. What is it?

answers.text: He has nothing to draw with
The well has gone completely dry
Samaritans are not allowed to share it

cards.question: The woman asks Jesus if He is greater than Jacob, who gave them this well.

cards.text: Jesus said to her, "Everyone who drinks this water will be thirsty again." It's like your phone at 100 percent in the morning that's BEGGING for the charger by three o'clock, like it hasn't seen you in YEARS.

cards.question: But the water Jesus gives is different. What happens to whoever drinks it?

answers.text: They will thirst once a year
They will thirst a little less

cards.question: Now the woman asks Jesus for this water. What reason does she give?

answers.text: So she won't keep coming here to draw
So she can carry it to her whole town
So she can give it to her livestock

cards.text: Then Jesus changes direction. Jesus told her, "Go, call your husband and come back."

cards.question: The woman tells Jesus that she has no husband.

cards.text: Jesus says she's correct. In fact, He tells her, she has had five husbands, and the man she has now is not her husband.

cards.question: Jesus knows her whole story without being told, so the woman says she can see that He is a ___.

cards.text: Then she brings up an old question between Samaritans and Jews. WHERE is a person supposed to worship?

cards.question: The woman says her fathers worshiped on this mountain, but the Jews say the place to worship is in ___.

cards.text: "Believe Me, woman," Jesus replied. A time is coming, He tells her, when they will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem, and He adds that salvation is from the Jews.

cards.question: Jesus says the time for this new kind of worship is still far off in the future.
If worship isn't about the mountain or Jerusalem, how does Jesus say the true worshipers will worship the Father?

cards.text: The woman says she knows the Messiah, called Christ, is coming, and when He comes, He will explain everything. Friend, that's like telling the delivery driver standing ON your porch, holding your box, that you're still waiting on your package.

cards.question: When the woman says the Messiah is coming, what does Jesus answer?

answers.text: I who speak to you am He
He will come in many years
You will meet Him in Jerusalem

cards.text: Just then His disciples come back, and they are surprised He's speaking with a woman. Picture them freezing in the doorway like they walked into the wrong meeting.

cards.question: One of the disciples asks Jesus, "Why are You talking with her?"

cards.text: Then the woman leaves her water jar and goes back into town. Friend, she came out here for WATER. And she leaves the JAR. That's leaving your car running in the parking lot because the news can't wait.

cards.question: Back in town, what does the woman tell the people?

answers.text: Come see a man who told me everything I ever did
Come see a prophet who gave me living water
Come see a teacher sitting by the old well

cards.question: The people of the town stay put and wait for Jesus to come to them.

cards.text: Meanwhile the disciples urged Him, "Rabbi, eat something." But He told them, "I have food to eat that you know nothing about."

cards.question: Jesus says He has food the disciples know nothing about. What do they ask one another?

answers.text: If He is planning to fast
If He went into town alone

cards.question: Jesus explains to His disciples what His food really is. What is it?

answers.text: To do the will of the One who sent Him
To rest with His disciples after a journey
To teach in the synagogues every Sabbath

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up something they say: "There are still four months until the harvest." But He tells them to lift up their eyes and look at the fields.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples the fields are already ripe for harvest.

cards.text: Jesus says the reaper is already gathering a crop for eternal life, so the sower and the reaper may rejoice together. Here the saying is true: 'One sows and another reaps.'

cards.question: So what does Jesus say He sent His disciples to reap?

answers.text: What they have not worked for
What they will plant next year

cards.text: Meanwhile, many of the Samaritans from that town believe in Jesus. And He hasn't even set foot in their town yet.

cards.question: At first, many Samaritans in the town believe in Jesus because of the woman's ___.

cards.text: So the Samaritans come out to Jesus and ask Him to stay with them. Not 'nice to meet You.' STAY.

cards.question: Jesus agrees and stays with the Samaritans for ___ days.

cards.text: And many more believe because of His message. The guest list just keeps growing.

cards.question: The Samaritans tell the woman they've heard Jesus for themselves. What do they now know He truly is?

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 9 quotes "There are still four months until the harvest.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question says Jesus passes through Samaria 'To get from Judea back to Galilee.' That gives a reason for why He had to pass through Samaria. John 4:4 says only that He had to, not why.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: This is the first time Jacob appears, and he isn't introduced. Joseph is called 'his son,' but the card never says who Jacob is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote, 'Hold on.' and 'The thirsty guy is now the one talking about GIVING water.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke calls Jesus 'The thirsty guy.' That makes Jesus the target of the humor.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: No card covers the rest of John 4:14, that the water becomes in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life. That is a key detail of the living water teaching.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Stop 2 is almost entirely flat retelling. Cards 1, 3, 5 and 7 have no humor or reactions, and the stop's only joke (card 10) gives away an answer. Papa Dorin reads like a pleasant narrator here, not laugh-out-loud funny.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The delivery driver joke (the driver is already on the porch holding the box) tells the baker that the Messiah is the one standing in front of her. That gives away card 11's answer, 'I who speak to you am He.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Stop 2's first three choice cards follow the same type pattern as Stop 1's first three (true/false, fill in the blank, fill in the blank). All three stops also open with a true/false card.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The joke has the disciples 'freezing in the doorway like they walked into the wrong meeting.' There is no doorway at the well, so the comparison is blended into the Bible scene.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The comparison 'because the news can't wait' gives a reason for why the woman left her jar. John 4:28 gives no reason.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'What they will plant next year' doesn't make sense, because nobody reaps what hasn't been planted yet. It isn't a believable choice.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says 'He hasn't even set foot in their town yet,' but John 4:5 says 'He came to a town of Samaria called Sychar.' The card also says 'Meanwhile,' a time link that John 4:39 doesn't give.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.
